# Fixed-platform air-gap capability

## Summary

The supplied-data engine calculates clearance and annual sampled breaches.
This invented platform demonstrates geometry only; it supplies no site or code evidence.

## Revision history

| Revision | Date | Change and reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial | 2026-11-05 | Demonstrate constant-rate forecasts and their limits. |
| 1 | 2026-11-06 | Clarify numerical equality and use evaluated subsidence in both tables. |

## Invented basis

All values are synthetic, in metres relative to one synthetic datum.
Reference deck underside is 10.0 m before any listed subsidence.
Supplied HAT is 1.5 m; supplied surge is 0.5 m; still water is their sum, 2.0 m.
Crest height above that still water is 3.0 m; required clearance is 1.0 m.
These values are arithmetic probes, not environmental or code criteria.
Real assessments must establish compatible datum, joint water-level and crest
conditions, return periods and required clearance independently for each case.

## Supplied subsidence history

These invented samples are cumulative downward movements from the reference deck.
The engine does not fit a rate to them.

| Year | Subsidence (m) | Clearance (m) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026 | 0.0 | 5.0 |
| 2028 | 1.0 | 4.0 |
| 2030 | 2.0 | 3.0 |

## Constant-rate annual forecast

Starting in 2030 with 2.0 m cumulative movement, the supplied rate is 0.5 m/year.
Samples are at the same annual anniversary; fractional-year crossings are not reported.
The water levels, crest and required clearance stay fixed throughout this example.

| Year | Subsidence (m) | Clearance (m) | Margin (m) | Meets supplied minimum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2030 | 2.0 | 3.0 | 2.0 | Yes |
| 2031 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 1.5 | Yes |
| 2032 | 3.0 | 2.0 | 1.0 | Yes |
| 2033 | 3.5 | 1.5 | 0.5 | Yes |
| 2034 | 4.0 | 1.0 | 0.0 | Yes |
| 2035 | 4.5 | 0.5 | -0.5 | No |
| 2036 | 5.0 | 0.0 | -1.0 | No |
| 2037 | 5.5 | -0.5 | -1.5 | No |
| 2038 | 6.0 | -1.0 | -2.0 | No |

First sampled breach: 2035. Equality meets the supplied minimum.
The comparison uses raw margin >= -1e-9 m, an absolute numerical rounding
tolerance only; clearance and margin are retained without adjustment.
This tolerance supplies no engineering allowance or general error bound.

## Engineering inputs to three options

| Option | Geometry supplied here | Work still needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Live with it | Annual margins and first sampled breach | Full wave-in-deck loads, structural assessment and justified manning or shut-in limits. |
| Raise the topside | Target-year 2038 clearance deficit: 2.0 m | Structural feasibility, uncertainties, interfaces, temporary works, lift procedure and independent assessment. |
| Decommission | Horizon and clearance deficit for comparison | Retirement feasibility, regulatory requirements and a separate business case. |

The deficit is max(0, minus target-year margin), a geometric input only.
It excludes uncertainty, changing environmental conditions and all structural or lift allowances.
It neither specifies a design lift height nor establishes feasibility of any option.
Costs and NPV are outside the engine.

## Limits and reproduction

No source-derived coefficients or published-case validation are established.
The referenced article was not retrieved from the attempted public address
